greeting: Good morning, Zuhair. It's been a stormy Saturday of voting in Victoria, so here's a clear catch-up.

lead.headline: Victoria heads into the count with Labor tipped to lose after 12 years
lead.summary: ABC analysts expected, before polls closed at 6pm Saturday, that Labor would be defeated barring an unprecedented polling miss, with the Coalition likely to win a majority. One Nation's rise makes some seats harder to call, and all 88 results may not be known until the second week of December. This edition was compiled before any results.

stories.headline: Google's quantum chip beats classical limits in a coordination game
stories.summary: In a Science paper dated 19 November, Google's team tested a quantum property called contextuality on tasks of up to 105 qubits. Google says its processor won the 'magic square' game 98.3% of the time, above the classical limit of about 88.9%, and the work has drawn tech press coverage.

stories.headline: One optical layer computes 100 functions at once
stories.summary: UCLA researchers report in Light: Science & Applications that a single light-shaping layer can calculate nonlinear functions without special nonlinear materials. In a visible-light test it handled 100 functions in one pass, and the work was in tech news this week.

stories.headline: Deep learning finds a heart-trace warning sign for sudden cardiac death
stories.summary: This Nature paper, back in the news this month, trained a model on more than 440,000 ECGs from Sweden and tested it on US and Taiwanese data. It picked out a higher-risk group than conventional measures did, which could one day help decide who gets an implanted defibrillator.

stories.headline: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secrets
stories.summary: OpenAI accuses Apple of stealing trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers. The filing answers Apple's July lawsuit, whose allegations OpenAI denies.

stories.headline: Banned Nvidia AI chips reportedly turn up in Shanghai
stories.summary: Citing Bloomberg's review of Chinese filings, The Decoder reports that two companies installed Blackwell hardware at a Shanghai data centre. Sending these chips to China without a US licence is banned.

stories.headline: AI shopping agents run into retailers' locked doors
stories.summary: Some retailers welcome AI agents, but Amazon blocks outside ones and others including eBay limit or block them. A Visa study found agents failed about 43% of test runs.

stories.headline: Storms close voting centres on election day
stories.summary: Flooding shut a voting centre at Keysborough Gardens Primary School, and heavy rain closed another in Wodonga. Earlier, the SES reported more than 400 callouts in 24 hours.

stories.headline: House collapses in McCrae landslide
stories.summary: The empty house on the Mornington Peninsula gave way after heavy rain. Neighbours were evacuated safely, no one was reported hurt, and emergency services warn the slope could move again.

stories.headline: North Melbourne seals an AFLW three-peat
stories.summary: The Kangaroos beat Melbourne in a thrilling grand final on Friday night to win their third premiership in a row.

stories.headline: Italy says drone in deadly Kuwait strike was made in Iran
stories.summary: Italy's foreign minister says Kuwaiti investigators have confirmed where the drone that killed two Italians was made. Iran denies launching it and has offered to join an inquiry.

stories.headline: Israeli strike on MSF clinic in Gaza kills two staff
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders says its clearly marked Gaza City clinic took a direct hit that killed two watchmen. Al Jazeera reports Israel's military claimed, without evidence, that they were Hamas members.

thought: Every count starts with a single ballot; patience beats the first projection.
